# Limited-domain working-record adoption (#160) {#working-record-160}

**On 2026-10-03 the investigator adopted the reviewed #160 F1″ candidate with its stated limits.** The [selected file](results/selected-current-best-parameters.json) is byte-identical to the [retained candidate](results/density-cp-160/D1-evidence/F1-double-prime-candidate-parameters.json), SHA-256 `756fec502d3a1433d538abb073c4caeabf91902013ab7e27d5459ce70396543b`. The active immutable Engine wheel is SHA-256 `48a639e78d00ef88a2f7e66ed1e3d89831ca0ad5267322330d44f48c34926060`, from Engine commit `464a9897615e513e5cc404ce5b49f46a72466d3d`. The candidate's document identity, purpose and “unpromoted candidate” wording remain frozen provenance. The [Stage 5 handoff](results/density-cp-160/stage5-absorber/handoff.json) likewise retains the producer's pre-adoption scope and wording. Today's decision changes the working-record selection; it does not relabel those historical checks or promote this notebook for manuscript use.

The intended working domain is **30 wt% MEA on a CO₂-free basis, 40–80 °C**. Pressure calibration is at 40/60 °C and species calibration at 20–60 °C; the 80 °C comparison is weaker. The [reviewed five-coordinate study](results/density-cp-160/D1-evidence/run-summary.json) retains original ion segment counts and the calibrated R2/R5 shifts. Corrected 141-target cost is **30.0897611888619** against #154's **33.03377424355485**, below **36.33715166791034**. Four fitted density states satisfy 1.6%, with absolute errors below **0.229%** in the absorber producer; pure-water Cp satisfies 3%. These are calibration, numerical verification and conditional comparison evidence.

The empirical volume translation is **density-only**. It uses native composition and equation-of-state volume to report corrected mass density; Engine `Parameters.from_mapping` does not apply it automatically. Native molar-density fields, chemical potentials, equilibrium, enthalpy and Cp keep their native meanings. The existing absorber #160 materialization already applies this correction explicitly.

One fixed **65-node, nine-film-point 3C** case passes its numerical and native-grid physical-certificate checks. Capture is **90.6093%** against **89.5%**; the **five-tap temperature RMSE is 3.4415 K** against 6 K, and maximum liquid temperature is **348.3281 K**. The two report-only solution-Cp misses are **+4.0103%** at nominal unloaded 318.15 K (loading-$10^{-5}$ proxy) and **−4.4927%** at loading 0.358 and 353.15 K, both at **7 mol MEA/kg water and assumed 101325 Pa**. Full #149 property acceptance is not established. These results retain estimated mobilities, an assumed 318.15 K liquid inlet, a provisional vapor caloric reference, the source gas basis and ambiguous tap phase. They establish no mesh independence, root uniqueness, propagated uncertainty or global physical validation. Concentration transfer and 100–120 °C qualification remain excluded.

Stages 1–4 and the common-wheel replay retain Supported reviews. Stage 5 was Supported for Amine handoff `d78373dccd5cd764e7d2fff6300fd87525a1df1f` against `41e4f91a4771d98f9d9492270c95588770a9dce1`, and absorber `bb70f6f7af62cdcdd029447cba34e44173a2750b` against `d26d368b4674ea8d5d390523c970eeaab44b2820`. The earlier #124 assessment received Supported review at `41e4f91a4771d98f9d9492270c95588770a9dce1`; checkpoint `fc4c0af9ece928010d76623bcc4b8cccbb3e2658` also contains the reviewed Stage 5 record. The [#124 comparison](results/density-cp-160/cp-124-assessment/summary.json) raises mean absolute saturated-water-density error from about **0.049% to 0.132%** on the primary grid. Its original joint requirements remain unchanged, unmet and open; this working-record adoption does not waive them.

The [history row](results/parameter-record-history.csv) records the actual replaced #154 selected SHA-256 `ae92bac5d2ef7ab690e692f6b1686e18cf06f24ac6b53a6aab4fafeb3046f1aa`. Previous history, YAML and current-map metadata stopped at #107 `9055458d` and omitted that replacement; this record assigns no prior adoption date. The following #154 and older sections preserve their original calculations and comparisons as historical evidence. No new fitting, absorber solve or numerical method was used for this adoption. Independent delivered review returned Supported for working-record adoption, notebook interpretation and rendered evidence at `14384ad0ea80f946acd15066ffeb41e35e8bd36a`, against `fc4c0af9ece928010d76623bcc4b8cccbb3e2658`, with the stated limits. # Final corrected-data rerun (#154, historical incumbent) {#final-rerun-154}

**SSM+DS F1 was the #154 selected calibrated record on the corrected 141-target base.** Its pressure/species costs are **8.438702 / 24.595073**, with fitted AARDs **13.9776% / 8.2582%**. The Born-off refit F3 raises those costs to **61.612150 / 35.026459** within the same five-coordinate bounds. This is bounded calibration and numerical verification, not physical necessity of the Born term or physical validation of the effective ion values.

This section supersedes the pre-correction fitted numbers in the retained studies below, including their former “working record” tables and density comparison. Those earlier studies do not describe the new selected record. This section and its render await independent delivered review and have not been promoted for manuscript use; the manuscript refresh is separate.

## Fixed basis and six fitted problems

The corrected packet and exact `strict141-targets.csv` identities from #152 supply **83 states: 47 pressure targets and 94 species targets**. F4/F5 add the **18 existing Matin HCO₃⁻ + CO₃²⁻ pool identities**, giving 159 targets and 112 species targets at the same states. Matin inputs remain source-unverified legacy observations at packet 20 °C; state 016 is display-only, excluded from both fit and 18-pool summaries. Böttinger aggregate operators are transported by the corrected packet, not counted again as independent species.

The pressure residual is $\ln(p_\mathrm{model}/p_\mathrm{obs})/0.3$; the species residual is $(x_\mathrm{model}-x_\mathrm{obs})/(0.1x_\mathrm{obs}+0.001)$. Costs are half the squared-residual sum. F1–F5 retain the `9055458d` chemistry, pure/ion/Born inputs and CO₂ $\epsilon/k=173.44$ K. The R2/R5 enthalpy shifts and R5 coefficient are calibration values tuned using data that included 80 °C. F6 instead fixes CO₂ $\epsilon/k=169.21$ K and the exact #140 source R2/R4/R5 inputs, with its reaction-`slope-fixed` structure and starts 1/2 (the MEAH⁺–water 1/T slope remains free).

Exactly **12 optimizer runs** converged. F1–F5 were retained without refitting; the two planned F6 runs used the existing #140 `feed_start` initialization. No Born-input, parameter-removal, fixed-interaction or heat refits were added. All two-start relative cost differences are below $7.3\times10^{-13}$, satisfying the $10^{-6}$ rule. Lower complete costs are reported; original Born remains the matched alternative, not a post-hoc replacement for primary SSM+DS.

## Conditional standard errors and replay

F1/F2 interior Jacobians have rank 4/4 and 3/3. The retained covariance uses $s^2(J_I^\mathsf{T}J_I)^{-1}$, physical-unit columns from optimizer scales 0.01 and 10 K, and $s^2=2\,\mathrm{cost}/(141-p)$ with each actual active-bound set. Variance factors are 0.4822448795 and 0.4948072134. At-bound coordinates have no symmetric interval.

| Problem | SE $k_{CW}$ | SE $k_{HW}$ | SE $k_{BW}$ | SE $k_{CH}$ | SE $b_{HW}$ / K |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|:--|--:|
| F1 | 0.013816 | 0.016560 | At bound | 0.027236 | 119.705816 |
| F2 | 0.013493 | 0.014596 | At bound | At bound | 108.636909 |

**F1's computed slope is −112.6 K with conditional SE 119.7 K.** This rerun does not change or remove that coordinate; any model change is a later owner decision. Unique F1 correlations (CW–HW, CW–CH, CW–slope, HW–CH, HW–slope, CH–slope) are −0.3785, 0.1431, 0.0849, 0.2495, 0.4592 and 0.0518. F2 correlations (CW–HW, CW–slope, HW–slope) are −0.4042, 0.1130 and 0.4183. [Full error](results/final-rerun/conditional-standard-errors.csv) and [correlation](results/final-rerun/conditional-correlations.csv) tables are unchanged from the initial result. Independent residuals are assumed despite shared-titration dependence; these errors are conditional and indicative only.

Every selected optimum reproduces its native cost within relative $9.44\times10^{-13}$, well inside $10^{-8}$. [Replay](results/final-rerun/evaluation/replay-checks.json) checks stationarity, element and charge balance and declared domain. The [uncertainty replay check](results/final-rerun/uncertainty-replay-checks.json) changes standard errors by at most $1.40\times10^{-14}$ relative and correlations by $2.22\times10^{-16}$; it does not refit parameters or recalculate the Jacobian.

## Born-off mechanism and pool effect

The unchanged #151 decomposition binds final F1 as `adopted` and F3 as `off-refit`, with the corrected 83-state/141-target mask, source-series cohorts, replay costs and SHA-256s. **N1–N9 all pass**. Across 47 pressure states, RMS $\Delta Q=1.094324$ exceeds RMS $\Delta S=0.819324$; the decomposed pressure-cost increase **53.1734487074** reproduces F3 minus F1. H1 is rejected (at nominal 40 °C, median overall Born reaction sum −0.905849; permittivity contribution at the median-loading state −0.287018). H2 is supported under the unchanged local rules: Spearman correlations −0.997067/−0.996429 and high-third ion contributions −1.759165/−1.749710 at nominal 40/60 °C. The activity-compensation criterion C is not rejected; high-third mean $\phi=(\Delta Q+Q_{\mathrm{Born,F1}})/Q_{\mathrm{Born,F1}}$ is 0.082522/−0.008930. Here $Q$ is the activity sum, $S$ the speciation sum and $H$ the vapor/reference correction, with $\Delta\ln p=\Delta Q+\Delta S+\Delta H$. These are outcomes of the tested decomposition and refits, not universal physical criteria.

![The tested Born-off refit changes the activity sum more than speciation in aggregate. Each marker is a computed state; no interpolation is implied. Grey shading is ±0.3 natural-log units, the declared pressure residual scale, not an acceptance interval. Nominal source-series labels do not replace the measured temperatures used in calculation.](results/final-rerun/figures/born-off-mechanism.png){#fig-final-born-off-mechanism}

Adding the legacy pool exposes a fit trade-off. On the common 141-target mask, F4/F5 costs rise to **37.642015 / 35.905010**, compared with F1/F2 **33.033774 / 34.141698**. Pool AARDs fall from **59.5875% / 34.9859%** to **42.5709% / 19.5581%**. The [pool-effect costs](results/final-rerun/figure-data/pool-effect-costs.csv) separate the 141-target base from the 18 added targets; totals with different target counts are not used to reselect Born form.

Four main-text data sets are retained without changing the manuscript: [pressure](results/final-rerun/figure-data/pressure.csv), [speciation](results/final-rerun/figure-data/speciation.csv), [Born-off plus mechanism](results/final-rerun/figure-data/born-off-mechanism.csv), and [pool effect](results/final-rerun/figure-data/pool-effect.csv). They contain discrete retained evaluations, not newly inferred continuous curves. The [decomposition checks](results/final-rerun/activity-contributions/checks.json) retain all errors and hypothesis outcomes.

The supported use remains a **calibrated model for 30 wt% MEA, pressure fitted at 40–60 °C and species at 20–60 °C**. Effective ion parameters, active bounds, conditional errors, reused high-temperature calibration information, legacy Matin inputs, concentration-transfer errors and loaded-density bias constrain interpretation. No heat fit, absorber qualification, unique physical identification or physical Born necessity is established. The wheel is unchanged: `28181e72e429c6e87fc6361082af1a7b21c8747e76bda65a1c30abb4a97402f2`.

# Independent chemical temperature estimates {#reaction-constants-140}

**The four-temperature source-only fits imply R4 hydrolysis enthalpy +13.179 kJ/mol and R5 dissociation enthalpy +50.555 kJ/mol. The R5 estimate corresponds to protonation enthalpy −50.555 kJ/mol, compared with Kim's measured heat-release magnitudes 49.0, 49.1 and 48.9 kJ/mol at 298.15, 313.15 and 333.15 K.** This stage is **diagnostic: source measurement uncertainty unavailable**. Chemical consistency under issue 140 remains **UNRESOLVED**; the comparison does not establish agreement within literature uncertainty.

The [Stage 2 preregistration](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-2-preregistration.md) was committed before fitting. The parent explicitly allowed residual-based covariance despite issue 140's source-uncertainty stop, while retaining its low-temperature selection, committed freeze and single-evaluation rules. Independent GPT-6 Astra readiness review returned **Ready** for this bounded diagnostic use at `2814df5`. The [input snapshot](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-2-inputs.json) retains exact rows from extraction commit `1e92af1` and matching live Zotero PDF hashes; no loaded-solution observation entered these chemical fits.

Aroua 1999 reaction (i) and Eqs. 1–2, p. 888, describe MEA + HCO₃⁻ ⇌ MEACOO⁻ + H₂O, exactly the reverse of R4. With 1 mol/L concentration and 1 mol/kg molality standards, the admitted infinite-dilution interpretation gives **K₄ᵐ=1/(ρw m° K₁,dim)**, where K₁,dim is in L/mol and ρw is in kg/L. No R2/R3/R5 combination is required. Water activity remains in the finite-solution R4 quotient; its unit limiting value belongs to the source's assumed infinite-dilution interpretation and is not guaranteed merely by zero ionic strength at finite neutral MEA concentration. The conversion reuses the Wagner–Pruss saturated-liquid water density correlation as a declared reference-density approximation, not an exact ambient-pressure conversion.

Kim 2011 §2.2, pp. 1755–1756, reports NBS-calibrated pH at half equivalence. The [IUPAC molal pH definition](https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/P04524) supports **ln K₅ᵐ=ln Ka,Kim**, without a mole-fraction offset or a factor of 55.51. The hydrated proton represents H₃O⁺−H₂O in the model reference; water activity remains in the finite-solution quotient. Kim §3.1, p. 1757, assumes dilute 0.01 mol/kg MEA constants equal infinite dilution based on an MDEA comparison, without independently verifying that approximation for MEA.

Both source fits use **ln K=A+B/T**, T in kelvin, with no C ln T or D T term. R4 uses Table 3 at 298/308/318/328 K, after density conversion; R5 uses only Kim Table 7 This work Exp at 298.15/313.15/323.15/333.15 K. Each centered linear least-squares fit has rank two and two residual degrees of freedom. The [coefficients and covariance](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-2/source-fit.json) and [source residuals](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-2/source-residuals.csv) retain all numerical values.

| Reaction | A | B / K | RMS ln K residual | Maximum absolute ln K residual | ΔH° / (kJ/mol) | Residual-based standard error of ΔH° / (kJ/mol) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| R4 hydrolysis | 2.282869879 | −1585.057202 | 0.0321833 | 0.0445803 | +13.1789 | 1.65385 |
| R5 dissociation | −1.443016604 | −6080.400894 | 0.0150079 | 0.0199123 | +50.5553 | 0.67618 |

The maximum R5 residual, **0.0199123 ln K**, is **0.4324 times** Kim's reported pH scale, 0.02 ln(10)=0.0460517 ln K, and **3.9825 times** the 0.005 ln K rounding half-step. These are descriptive comparisons with reported scales, whose coverage and covariance are unknown; they do not establish agreement within measurement uncertainty. Chemical consistency remains **UNRESOLVED**.

For coefficient order (A,B), the residual-based covariance matrices are

$$
\operatorname{Cov}_4=\begin{pmatrix}0.40541430&-126.57075\\-126.57075&39566.05474\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_5=\begin{pmatrix}0.06619252&-20.90547\\-20.90547&6613.79015\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Their diagonal units are dimensionless² and K²; off-diagonal entries have units K. The (A,B) coefficient correlations are −0.99936 and −0.99915; the centered (ln K(313.15 K),B) covariance is retained separately to avoid interpreting coordinate correlation as missing source-fit rank. Covariance assumes independent equal-variance residuals and uses their fitted variance; it does not estimate unreported systematic error or campaign correlation. The fitted reaction enthalpy is −RB. These few scalar coefficients and exact covariance values are shown in tables and equations because a plot would not further resolve their statistical meaning.

The fitted R5 heat-release magnitude exceeds the three low-temperature measurements by **1.5553, 1.4553 and 1.6553 kJ/mol**, respectively. Kim reports ±2.5% experimental heat uncertainty, giving stated scales 1.2250, 1.2275 and 1.2225 kJ/mol, without a coverage factor or measurement covariance. The [enthalpy comparison](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-2/protonation-enthalpy-comparison.csv) keeps those source scales separate from the residual-based fitted standard error. No uncertainty-qualified chemical pass is claimed. Kim's finite-concentration calorimetry is assumed infinite dilution in its §3.1; it measures protonation, not R4 hydrolysis.

The [finite-ionic-strength check](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-2/finite-I-loading-scatter.csv) reports all 16 temperature/added-salt groups of Aroua Table 2. Across each group's three loadings, Kc ranges span **0.85–3.55 L/mol**. Those loadings are not replicate measurements, and their total ionic strengths differ. Reliable total ionic strengths are not tabulated; the method-derived species table has inconsistent printed fields. The rows therefore do not support reproducing scatter of the four zero-I constants. This finite-I loading spread supplies no missing Table 3 measurement covariance.

The [native coefficient checks](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-2/native-coefficient-checks.csv) verify the source-to-native coefficient algebra at all eight source temperatures within the existing 5×10⁻¹³ ln K tolerance. R5 maps to the existing pKa-polynomial input using a=−B/ln(10), b=−A/ln(10), c=0. R2 stays at its source correlation and R1/R3 remain unchanged. Source correlation and coefficient algebra are numerical estimation and verification; neither establishes physical validation.

## Numerical evidence and permitted use

All **578 new assessment states** passed requested Engine tolerance and reported no balance errors; maximum absolute stationarity residual is **2.27374×10⁻¹³**, below 10⁻¹⁰. The existing 23 adopted Wagner states and 113 adopted heat states were reused, not recalculated. Effective k(T)<1 checks remain satisfied at fitting, 353.15 and 393.15 K endpoints. Exact checks, parameter hashes and numerical completeness remain in the stage JSON files and [result summary](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-2/stage-2-summary.json). Numerical verification does not establish uncertainty-qualified chemistry or physical validation.

The bounded finding is that independent diagnostic R4/R5 point estimates, followed by ≤60 °C loaded-solution estimation, preserve low-T cost and modestly reduce Phase B errors, but fail the adopted 80 °C pressure no-loss condition. The result is conditional on the historical SSM+DS model, transferred parameters and CO₂–water/MEA–water binary interactions estimated using higher-temperature binary data. The covariance of independent source fits is not propagated into the fixed-chemistry loaded-solution estimates. Source uncertainty and chemical consistency remain UNRESOLVED; active interaction bounds and two local starts limit identification. Independent GPT-6 Astra delivered review returned **Supported at `887e078` relative to `cc508d1`** for this diagnostic use, after one presentation correction round. It independently reproduced the source coefficients/covariance, eight fit costs and selection, pressure and heat metrics, Matin report-only values, frozen hashes and exact adopted-baseline reuse. All 16 new rendered evidence links resolve to byte-identical retained sources. Source chemical consistency remains UNRESOLVED; investigator promotion for manuscript use is pending and no new record is adopted. The authorized numerical stage is complete.


# Source-constant temperature control {#temperature-reanchor-140}

**The source-constant control preserves low-temperature family costs but fails the 80 °C no-loss pressure condition: primary AARD 29.333590% versus 20.270257%. Both frozen records also underpredict the never-accessed Wagner pressures.** The [preregistration](results/temperature-reanchor-140/preregistration.md) froze the owner-directed [issue 140](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/140) control before readiness review and fitting. Its inputs preserve 48 pressure targets at 40/60 °C and 94 species targets at 20–60 °C, the existing diagnostic scales and the Matin measured-21 °C/packet-20 °C convention.

The fresh replay on Engine wheel `28181e72` with selected record `9055458d…` gives **32.991897261221126**, differing from the required reference by **−7.11×10⁻¹⁵** (absolute tolerance 10⁻⁸). Pressure/species costs are **8.14345313051485/24.848444130706277**. All 84 states met the requested tolerance, with no reported balance errors and maximum stationarity residual **3.98×10⁻¹³**. [Exact target predictions and residuals](results/temperature-reanchor-140/replay-targets.csv) and [replay diagnostics](results/temperature-reanchor-140/replay.json) retain the numerical evidence. This verifies replay of the chosen calculation; it does not provide new physical validation.

The [restored default candidate](results/temperature-reanchor-140/restored-source-parameters.json) resets R2/R4/R5 completely to their published source laws, restores CO₂ dispersion energy to **169.21 K**, and sets the four free interaction intercepts and optional MEAH⁺–water slope to default zeros. It does not import the adopted fitted vector as an optimizer start. Other fixed parameters remain under the explicitly disclosed [selection-ancestry audit](results/temperature-reanchor-140/fixed-parameter-ancestry.csv). The source reset and later low-temperature estimation are separate operations; [parameter changes](results/temperature-reanchor-140/parameter-changes.csv) retain each reset.

The following dimensionless ln K values are all on the common aqueous-molality infinite-dilution basis. R1–R3 come from Austgen 1991 Table V, p. 547, including the +8.033069984598958/+4.016534992299479/+4.016534992299479 basis offsets; R4 is Tong 2012 Table 5, p. 44, via Aroua 1999; R5 is the complete Bates–Pinching source law, also reproduced to rounding in Böttinger 2008 Table 5, p. 138. The native C ln(T/Tref) input uses the corresponding A transform at Tref=313.15 K. Source PDFs and reading-copy hashes were checked as specified in the preregistration. A fresh local Bates PDF download was refused; the official NIST text was read, and its locally recorded hash was not refreshed.

This finite algebraic check is represented by a lookup table; a curve would not add evidence about conversion error. Agreement checks the coefficient/basis algebra, not the full reaction-to-EOS reference transformation or the physical uncertainty of extrapolated chemistry. Böttinger's printed R5 coefficients differ from the exact Bates law by ≤**1.54×10⁻⁵ in ln K** at these temperatures, as retained in the [rounding comparison](results/temperature-reanchor-140/r5-source-rounding.csv).

The [training targets](results/temperature-reanchor-140/training-targets.csv) and [assessment identities](results/temperature-reanchor-140/assessment-row-ids.json) are frozen before fitting. The four structures cross constant k versus the existing one-slope k(T) with source-fixed versus one fitted constant CO₂ energy; two source/default starts each allow at most eight fits. The 1% low-temperature cost rule yields at most one finalist per energy branch. The primary is the numerically complete finalist with the fewest fitted coordinates, with ties favoring fixed source energy. If the other energy branch also has a complete finalist, both records are exported and frozen before 80 °C access; the other record is a prespecified secondary comparison. Model selection remains unresolved until the deferred temperature folds. Neither record, role nor weights can change on the basis of 80 °C scores.

The completed single assessment stage scored the primary and frozen secondary on the same **21 canonical 80 °C pressure rows**, the identical **19-row comparison**, and **all 11 admitted 80 °C species targets**. The **57 rows at 100–120 °C**, **33/37 rows at 15/45 wt%**, and finite-dose heat comparisons remain outside selection and the fitting objective. The fixed CO₂–water k=0.013262879176919628 comes from all 39 Kiepe binary rows at 313.20/353.11/373.26/393.17 K (Engine `1ed0d0bc`, physical-co2-water `result.json:182`); fixed MEA–water k=−0.07352749874985018 comes from a 25-row Cai binary fit over 362.81–431.85 K (Engine `186e816`, neutral-mea-water `results/neutral-mea-water.json:4157`). Both are known high-temperature binary-subsystem fits retained by the owner; fixed model/association/dielectric choices previously had high-temperature access, whereas the May pure-ion numerical fit used only 20/40/60 °C rows. Any resulting temperature extrapolation is conditional on these disclosed historical fixed choices. There is no new untouched physical validation, concentration-transfer or stripper-use claim.

The independent readiness review supported the conversions, Wagner admission and frozen selection/numerical rules, while identifying high-temperature binary-subsystem ancestry. ## Stage 3 design amendment: hydration approximation and wheel replays

The [amended Stage 3 preregistration](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-3-preregistration.md) retains independent Plummer–Busenberg R2 as primary and free R2 a/b as secondary, with seven fits maximum and no fit executed yet. The parent must obtain a short independent re-review before fitting. No new loaded ≥80 °C state was evaluated.

PB explicitly defines dissolved CO2 as CO2⁰+H2CO3⁰ (p. 1012, Eq. 5); the unavailable Edwards 1978 full text leaves its convention unverified. Under the parent's 0.5% rule, both laws use the combined pool as a disclosed approximation. Using [Wang et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp909019u), Tables 1–2 p. 1737, take r25∈[0.0013,0.0017] and hydration enthalpy H∈[6,14] kJ/mol, a rectangular envelope twice the printed uncertainties, and r(T)=r25 exp[H/R(1/298.15−1/T)]. The [retained hydration table](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-3/hydration-bound.csv) gives maxima on 293–353.15 K: r≤0.0040967021, ln(1+r)≤0.0040883334, and RT² d ln(1+r)/dT≤0.057119826 kJ/mol. Thus the K correction is ≤0.40967021% under that continuation, below the parent's limit. The paper measures only 6.6–42.8 °C; extrapolation with constant enthalpy and constant-water concentration is an engineering assumption, not an empirical whole-interval bound or confidence interval. Unknown curvature and the nonlinear pressure response remain outside this bound. No claim that a near-threshold pressure result is insensitive to the convention is established.

### Secondary enthalpy interpretation and limits

The secondary fits δL0=+0.14510621 and δH=−5.90480665 kJ/mol relative to source Austgen at 313.15 K. Starts differ by 1.82202×10⁻⁸ in δL0 and 1.01278×10⁻⁶ kJ/mol in δH. Both R2 coordinates are interior, seven-column scaled/normalized Jacobians have full numerical rank, and R2 a/b versus interaction-slope column correlations are −0.39930/−0.37429, below 0.95. These explicit registered identification-falsifier tests are not triggered. R2 a/b columns themselves correlate at +0.999378; normalized smallest singular value is 0.00891855 versus maximum 2.04042.

Two interaction intercepts are at bounds: MEAH+–water −0.5 and HCO3−–water +0.5. The driver conservatively withholds `R2_identified` and unconditional transformed R2 covariance whenever any coordinate is at a bound, a stricter condition than the registered R2-bound test. It does not mean an R2 bound was reached. The [conditional R2 diagnostics](results/temperature-reanchor-140/stage-3/secondary-conditional-R2-diagnostics.json) transform the frozen conditional covariance with these interaction coordinates held fixed. In order (δL0, δH in kJ/mol), the matrix is [[0.00384685, −0.04258456], [−0.04258456, 19.01898142]], yielding local standard errors 0.0620230 and 4.36108 kJ/mol. These residual-based diagnostic scales are not measurement confidence intervals and exclude active-bound, model and source uncertainty. The shift is conditional mixture calibration, without a claim of independently identified physical R2 enthalpy.

The supported claim is bounded prediction failure under the admitted conventions. Edwards' combined CO2+H2CO3 convention remains assumed because full text is unavailable. The hydration envelope relies on constant-enthalpy continuation beyond Wang's measured 42.8 °C and is not an empirical whole-interval bound. Source uncertainty, compression, source pressure, active bounds and model discrepancy remain distinct. The 100–120 °C scores use a frozen continuation outside the candidate temperature domain; historical high-temperature binary interactions/model choices remain. R4/R5 chemical consistency is unresolved, concentration/stripper use is not qualified, and no parameter or manuscript result is adopted.

# Model D: historical 160-target assessment {#model-d-decision23}

**Both Born forms meet the accepted 104-row pressure rule and numerical-completeness checks.** The average absolute relative deviation (AARD) at 40–80 °C is **21.04 % for SSM+DS** and **20.50 % for Original Born**, against the owner’s 35 % limit. This comparison does not select a parameter record. Large errors on the 15 and 45 mass% MEA second-look rows, active bounds in Original Born, and the limits below prevent interpreting the pass as physical validation or qualification for absorber or stripper calculations.

This historical section reports [MEA #121 decisions 20–23](https://github.com/tannerpolley/MEA-Thermodynamics/issues/121#issuecomment-5896373779) and the [accepted recovery](https://github.com/tannerpolley/MEA-Thermodynamics/issues/121#issuecomment-5901117598). The following 160-target fits and comparison tables retain their original identities. The selected-parameter tables and regenerated pressure, speciation and heat figures later in this notebook now describe the 142-target `p5conv-a-11` working record. Its objective omits the 18 report-only Matin bicarbonate-pool targets.

## Model, data, and fitting controls

The two S1 forms use the same five adjustable coordinates: carbamate–water, MEAH⁺–water, and HCO₃⁻–water interaction coefficients, the MEAH⁺–MEACOO⁻ interaction coefficient, and the reciprocal-temperature slope of MEAH⁺–water. The first three coefficients have bounds ±0.5, the cation–anion coefficient ±1, and the slope ±1000 K. At $T_\mathrm{ref}=313.15$ K,

$$
k_{\mathrm{MEAH^+,water}}(T)=k_{\mathrm{MEAH^+,water}}(T_\mathrm{ref})
+b(1/T-1/T_\mathrm{ref}).
$$

R4 stays at its source correlation, $\ln K_4=2.151-1545.3/T$; R1–R3, R5, the remaining interaction coefficients, and species parameters stay at the recorded base values. SSM+DS uses effective Born coefficients $c_\mathrm{shell}=c_\mathrm{dielectric}=1$; Original Born uses explicit zeros. The SSM base document omits the two keys and the retained loader supplies (1, 1); the Original Born document supplies (0, 0). [Bases, candidates, and complete wheel identities](model-d/decision23-candidate-identities.json) identify this distinction.

Decision 23 fits **160 targets at 84 states**: 48 pressure targets (32 at 40 °C, 16 at 60 °C) and 112 liquid mole-fraction targets (84 at 20 °C, 16 at 40 °C, 12 at 60 °C). The weighted objective is half the sum of squared residuals, using $\ln(p_\mathrm{calc}/p_\mathrm{obs})/0.3$ for pressure and $(x_\mathrm{calc}-x_\mathrm{obs})/(0.1x_\mathrm{obs}+0.001)$ for species. Bicarbonate observations use the retained HCO₃⁻ + CO₃²⁻ pool. Böttinger 042/046 and Matin 016 remain excluded. The 80 °C isotherm stays outside the objective.

The accepted method is the existing Engine Ceres Levenberg–Marquardt fit with exact implicit derivatives, coordinate scales 0.01 and 10 K, 100 iterations and 7200 s per start. The function tolerance remains $10^{-12}$. Six prescribed starts per form include the old-rule optimum, C_src, pre-refit, incumbent-R4-C, and random seeds 1 and 2. The current admissibility check uses 293.15–353.15 K; this is narrower than decision 20’s historical 293.15–393.15 K check. Values at 393.15 K are retained for reporting and do not extend qualification.

Decision 23 removed 100–120 °C pressure targets from the objective and replaced the earlier all-temperature pressure and Mamun requirements with AARD ≤35 % on the 104 canonical 40–80 °C rows, retaining numerical completeness. The change followed the old-rule comparison: both forms passed the old pooled-pressure rule but failed its Mamun requirement. The owner narrowed the intended temperature domain; the retained 100–120 °C rows now report extrapolation. The [old-rule results](model-d/README.md#old-rule-all-temperatures-mamun-gate-s1-results) retain that chronology. No S2 fit is needed under the accepted S1 pass rule.

## Published pressure comparison and claim limits

Akula et al. report 40.5 % unweighted pressure MAPE for 30 mass% MEA, loading 0.003–0.5 and 40–120 °C ([Akula 2023a](#ref-18), p. 10 §4.2, Eq. 36). Its measured-pressure denominator matches the AARD calculation here, but the paper does not give the scored row count, row list, or calculated pressures. Its Table 3 (p. 8) lists pressure-calibration sources Aronu, Hilliard, Jou, Xu, and Kim; Figure 4 (p. 12) instead displays Aronu, Hilliard, Jou, Mamun, and Kim. The present 106-row subset contains Aronu 34, Hilliard 26, Jou 31, and Xu 15, and omits Kim and Mamun. Thus the values 27.86/25.80 % cannot establish superior performance on the same observations. The subset also includes this study’s out-of-range 100–120 °C calculations.

Akula jointly fits pressure and heat in Eq. 34 (weights 1 and 0.2), while its speciation comparisons are outside that fit (p. 11 and Figure 7, p. 14). Model D instead fits 112 species targets as well as 48 pressure targets. The differing data use prevents calling these species comparisons equivalent prediction tests. The source read for this comparison is Zotero RVYVQKSF/IIYKTEG7, PDF SHA-256 `08f429473719f766ea5d8fb370de310d7e81da94039bf23ce779d92a131d68d3`; its absent ignored reading copy did not make the primary paper unavailable.

Both historical 160-target forms passed the owner’s screening rule; that historical comparison adopted neither record and established no absorber/stripper physical validation. The later 142-target decision is stated below. The held-out 80 °C comparisons are outside the fit but were inspected in earlier studies; the 100–120 °C comparisons are extrapolations. This recovery does not establish new caloric performance, confidence intervals, matched-run speedup, or the cause of the historical 60-iteration plateaus. The retained assessment was covered by the [Supported delivered review](https://github.com/tannerpolley/MEA-Thermodynamics/issues/121#issuecomment-5907883147); the new promotion/views await separate review.

# Born-form comparison: SSM+DS vs Original Born {#born-form-comparison}

**The Born-form ranking depends on which species observations enter the fit.** Original Born has the lower cost on the historical 160-target objective, 40.201537 against 47.625767 for SSM+DS. After removing Matin's 18 bicarbonate-pool targets, the converged 142-target fits favor SSM+DS, 32.991897 against 34.584032. Both forms are reported here. This is an application of the modified Born term to reactive MEA–CO₂–H₂O extending [Figiel et al. (2025)](#ref-10), whose parameter estimation and results concern ion solvation, salt activities and aqueous/organic solvent mixtures (Model Parameters, Tables 2–5; Results, Figs. 4–9). It does not establish an intrinsic ranking of the two Born forms.

The historical 160-target calculations, the 142-target sensitivity fits and the exploratory reaction fits have different data or adjustable coordinates. They are distinguished throughout. The preceding decision-23 assessment concerns the older 160-target records; the completed numerical assessment of the 142-target records is reported below. The <a href="model-d/born-form-diagnosis/diagnosis.qmd" download="diagnosis.qmd">detailed diagnosis.qmd record</a> retains the original probes; <a href="model-d/born-form-diagnosis/p5conv-results.qmd" download="p5conv-results.qmd">the convergence record</a> retains the later P4/P5 fits. Both use numerical evidence from installed wheel `28181e72e429c6e87fc6361082af1a7b21c8747e76bda65a1c30abb4a97402f2`.

## Formulation and question

The question is whether the SSM+DS cost penalty in this MEA application follows from the inherited Born diameters, solvent factors, dielectric-saturation correction, or reduced composition sensitivity after the five interaction coordinates are fitted. SSM means the solvation-shell modification; DS means dielectric saturation. The implemented relations are the Engine equations `born_outer_shell_diameter`, `born_radial_charging_work` and `born_residual_helmholtz`:

$$
f_{\mathrm{mix}}=\frac{\sum_k x_k f_k}{\sum_k x_k},\qquad
D_i=d_i^{\mathrm{Born}}\left[1+c_{\mathrm{shell}}\frac{f_{\mathrm{mix}}-1}{|z_i|}\right],
$$

$$
W_{\mathrm{Born}}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}x_i z_i^2
\left[\frac{1-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{bulk}}^{-1}}{D_i}
+c_{\mathrm{dielectric}}(1-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ion}}^{-1})
\left(\frac1{d_i^{\mathrm{Born}}}-\frac1{D_i}\right)\right],
\qquad
a^{\mathrm{Born}}=-\frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 k_B T}W_{\mathrm{Born}}.
$$

Here $a^{\mathrm{Born}}$ is the dimensionless residual Helmholtz contribution, $z_i$ is ionic charge number and $\mathcal I$ is the set of ions. Distances are expressed in consistent units, with metres in the SI prefactor; the retained diameter parameters are in Å. SSM+DS is $(c_{\mathrm{shell}},c_{\mathrm{dielectric}})=(1,1)$ and Original Born is $(0,0)$. At $c_{\mathrm{shell}}=0$, $D_i=d_i^{\mathrm{Born}}$, so the saturation correction vanishes; the retained equality evaluation verifies that $(0,1)$ equals $(0,0)$.

Figiel's Born Term, Eqs. (5)–(10), pp. 9407–9409, provides the shell and solvation-factor construction; Table 1, p. 9409, gives $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ion}}=8$, and Model Parameters, Table 2, p. 9411, gives $f_{\mathrm{water}}=1.5$. The Engine equation record attributes its canonical charging form to corrected Eq. (7); the correction text was not separately verified in this source reading. The installed Engine averages $f_k$ over all nine components, including ions. With the baseline $f_{\mathrm{MEA}}=1$ and unit factors for CO₂ and the ions, $f_{\mathrm{mix}}=1+0.5x_{\mathrm{water}}$. Consequently, the shell diameter depends on ionic content and the Born contribution can enter water activity. Model D retains solvent-only bulk permittivity; it does not add explicit ion suppression to that mixing rule.

## Fit basis and source methods

The historical fit uses **160 targets at 84 declared states**, with a CO₂-free feed basis of **30 wt% MEA in water**: 48 pressure targets at 40/60 °C, 40 Böttinger species targets and 72 Matin species targets. The same five interaction coordinates and bounds are used for the two forms. The weights define dimensionless residuals and cost:

$$
r_p=\frac{\ln(p_{\mathrm{calc}}/p_{\mathrm{obs}})}{0.3},\qquad
r_x=\frac{x_{\mathrm{calc}}-x_{\mathrm{obs}}}{0.1x_{\mathrm{obs}}+0.001},\qquad
C=\frac12\sum_j r_j^2.
$$

The species targets are liquid mole fractions; a positive signed residual means the model lies above the observation. The bicarbonate target uses the retained HCO₃⁻ + CO₃²⁻ pool. These weights are the declared fitting scales, not independently measured experimental standard deviations. The 80 °C isotherm is outside this fit. P1 additionally describes the 15 and 45 wt% states on common composition paths; those descriptive probes do not enlarge the fitted domain.

[Matin et al. (2012)](#ref-6) use acid/base titration, total alkalinity and CO₂ loading at ambient pressure and temperature (Experimental Section, pp. 6614–6615; supplementary Table S1). Their figures label the measurements **21 °C**; the retained packet uses **20 °C**. Their Speciation Comparisons discussion reports bicarbonate above Jakobsen's NMR values, especially at loading 0.3–0.45 (Fig. 2, p. 6616), and compares their 21 °C results with Böttinger's 20 °C results (Fig. 3, p. 6617). Their MEA, MEAH⁺ and carbamate comparisons are closer to NMR. This source-method distinction is retained rather than correcting the data by the fitted residual.

[Böttinger et al. (2008)](#ref-8) use online quantitative ¹H/¹³C NMR (§3, pp. 132–134; MEA results in §7, Figs. 6–7). Fast proton exchange permits measurement of **MEA + MEAH⁺ as a sum**, rather than separate free and protonated MEA observations. Bicarbonate is quantified by ¹³C NMR, and the authors describe carbonate as practically absent under their conditions. Different measurement methods, temperatures, loading coverage and reported species prevent treating the residual signs alone as proof of experimental inconsistency.

## Born activity contributions and local hypotheses

P1 evaluates Born chemical-potential differences at identical temperature, density and composition and subtracts the infinite-dilution pure-water reference at 101325 Pa. Its reaction quantity is the dimensionless Born part of $\sum_i\nu_i\ln\gamma_i$. On the common 30 wt% composition path at 313.15 K, the changes over the retained loading range are:

| Reaction | Original Born on its path | SSM+DS on that same path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | -1.414296 | -2.610798 |
| R2 | -1.425040 | -2.163867 |
| R3 | -2.235989 | -2.973947 |
| R4 | +0.556367 | -0.172566 |
| R5 | -0.040186 | -0.819822 |

The magnitudes increase for R1–R3 and R5 in SSM+DS, while R4 decreases and changes sign. **P1 therefore shows no uniform attenuation of reaction activity sensitivity.** The 15 and 45 wt% common-path tables retain the additional concentration dependence. The simple per-ion charging-kernel ratio $d_i/D_i$ is not the full reaction sensitivity.

The Born part of $\ln a_{\mathrm{water}}$ and its SSM+DS − Original difference were evaluated at each Matin and Böttinger state, both at their own compositions and on the common composition path. For the 18 fitted Matin bicarbonate targets, its rank correlation with the weighted residual difference is **0.733746**; the common-path calculation gives the same rank correlation. Including the report-only retained Matin state gives **0.773684, n = 19**. The common path separates the composition-coupling association from a speciation shift, but **this remains descriptive association, not causal attribution**. [Per-state activities](model-d/born-form-diagnosis/p1-matin-bottinger-born-activities.csv), [correlations](model-d/born-form-diagnosis/p1-rank-correlations.csv) and [the association plot](model-d/born-form-diagnosis/matin-water-activity-association.svg) retain the decomposition.

P2 uses exact Engine interaction columns and two-step finite-difference Born-input columns, with relative steps $10^{-4}$ and $10^{-5}$, pointwise agreement tolerance $10^{-3}\max(|J_1|,|J_2|)+10^{-8}$ and one larger-step retry. No entry is dropped or zeroed; a column that still disagrees is unavailable. Bounds are engineering analog envelopes from Figiel's Model Parameters, Tables 2–3, p. 9411: 2–5 Å for the non-proton ions, 1–2 Å for H₃O⁺ and 1–2 for $f_{\mathrm{MEA}}$, with local displacements at most half the interval width. These are not measured MEA-ion bounds. The declared reduction screens are 3.71 cost units for at least half of the original gap, below 1.86 for not supported locally, and an inconclusive band between them.

| Hypothesis | Retained P2/P3 finding | Classification against the declared falsifier |
|:--|:--|:--|
| (a) Inherited Born diameters account for the gap | Main-ion local prediction: 4.072221 reduction; confirming five-interaction refit converged at 43.950877, a 3.674890 reduction, below 3.71. The secondary-ion group includes an unavailable H₃O⁺ derivative. | **Inconclusive**; at least half accounted for was not confirmed. |
| (b) Shell/MEA solvation-factor directions account for the gap | Bounded local predicted reduction 3.072805; no confirming refit under the accepted best-group selection. | **Inconclusive**. |
| (c) The dielectric-saturation correction accounts for the gap | Local saturation-direction reduction is zero (**not supported locally**); (0,1) = (0,0) is verified, but the (1,0) comparison has no complete objective. | **Unavailable** for the finite-form comparison. |
| (d) Reduced composition sensitivity explains the remaining gap | P1 shows no uniform attenuation; unavailable and unconfirmed parameter groups prevent the proposed elimination argument. | **Inconclusive**. |

The H₃O⁺ column has only 157 of 160 entries agreeing after its retry, so the joint P2/P3 group is unavailable. This derivative-quality result is distinct from a failed equilibrium solve and supplies no physical falsification. [Screening table](model-d/born-form-diagnosis/p2-screening.csv), [step agreement](model-d/born-form-diagnosis/p2-step-agreement.csv) and [confirming refit](model-d/born-form-diagnosis/p3-best-group-confirmation.json) retain the numerical basis.

The five final interaction coordinates are the exact P5 values in the selected record and [fit result](model-d/born-form-diagnosis/p5conv-a-11-results.json). For MEAH⁺–water, $k(T)=k+b(1/T-1/313.15\,\mathrm{K})$, with $k=-0.37931089293768305$ and $b=-148.5346444297559$ K. HCO₃⁻–water is at its +0.5 upper bound. The source R4 correlation is $\ln K_4=2.151-1545.3\,\mathrm{K}/T$ on the common aqueous-molality basis; R1–R3/R5 retain the assessed source corrections and inherited shifts. Effective R1–R5 equality is retained in the [identity check](results/promotion-107-identity.json).

## Reaction directions and converged Matin-role fits

P4 adds carbamate and bicarbonate offset and enthalpy directions, with $\delta$ a natural-log equilibrium-constant shift at 313.15 K and $\Delta H$ in kJ/mol:

$$
\Delta\ln K(T)=\delta-\frac{1000\Delta H}{R}(1/T-1/313.15),
\qquad |\delta|\leq1,\quad |\Delta H|\leq10\;\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}.
$$

The reduced directions are carbamate R2 − R4 − R5 and bicarbonate R2 − R5. They map to recorded reaction changes $\Delta R2=\mathrm{bicarbonate}$ and $\Delta R4=\mathrm{bicarbonate}-\mathrm{carbamate}$, for both offsets and enthalpies. R1, R3 and R5 remain fixed and all nine species remain in the equilibrium calculation. Reaction gradients have **finite-difference quality**, alongside exact Engine interaction gradients; no covariance is estimated.

The later P4 warm refits freed the five interaction coordinates and all four reaction coordinates. Their returned full-objective costs are **43.67 for SSM+DS and 32.29 for Original Born**:

| Form | Full 160 cost | Pressure | Böttinger | Matin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SSM+DS | 43.665318 | 9.526312 | 5.325559 | 28.813446 |
| Original Born | 32.289167 | 8.736058 | 6.125182 | 17.427927 |

| Form | Carbamate δ | Carbamate ΔH, kJ/mol | Bicarbonate δ | Bicarbonate ΔH, kJ/mol |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SSM+DS | 0.195560 | 10.000000 | 0.080762 | 4.911380 |
| Original Born | 0.369794 | 10.000000 | 0.720019 | -0.871919 |

Both stopped at the remaining-time guard after four accepted steps and four complete Jacobians, **without convergence**. The carbamate $\Delta H$ reaches its **+10 kJ/mol bound in both**. The last accepted point has a complete objective but no new Jacobian. All 32 completed reaction columns pass the agreement rule; one SSM+DS bicarbonate enthalpy column required the permitted retry. The source-correlation combinations before EOS conversion are not measured reduced-reaction constants or absorption heats. These unfinished local fits leave Original Born lower on the full data, but do not establish a converged reaction-adjusted ranking.

P5 changes the fitted target set while keeping the five interaction bounds and weights, source reactions and Born inputs fixed. All four warm fits converged on the native relative function tolerance $10^{-12}$, with zero or one further accepted update from the capped records. **HCO₃⁻–water is at its +0.5 bound in every P5 fit**; Original Born also reaches the cation–anion −1 bound.

## Unavailable solves and limits

The two unavailable cases reproduce exactly on the pinned wheel at 313.15 K: the (1,0) shell-only target at `vle_obs_0119`, and scan B at $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ion}}=2$ at `vle_obs_0193`. [tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT#201](https://github.com/tannerpolley/ePC-SAFT/pull/201) reports the conserved-carbon balance (row 16) as the failing row in both; case 1 also fails the total-MEA balance. Continuation along the sampled branches turns back before each target: near $c_{\mathrm{dielectric}}=0.33$ for case 1 and $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ion}}=2.018$–2.031 for case 2, with a returning segment above 2.

Along those branches the dimensionless Born contribution becomes more negative, from about −5 to −17 in case 1 and −22 to −52 in case 2; OH⁻ in case 1 or H₃O⁺ in case 2 reaches about 0.8–1 mol%. Bounded Newton probes and alternate starts found no criterion-meeting target root. The Engine report classifies both states as having **undetermined global existence**: disconnected solutions are not excluded, neither failure establishes physical nonexistence, and neither is proved to be a solver failure at an existing target solution. Its fix-before-negative investigation **remains open**, and no Engine runtime repair was made. Both cases therefore remain **unavailable for attribution, with an undetermined cause**; they do not rank the fitted forms and are not evidence about either Born form. The frozen requests and parameters remain in [engine-handoff/](model-d/born-form-diagnosis/engine-handoff/).

The completed values are **numerical verification and local fitting evidence, not physical validation**. They do not establish an intrinsic ranking, concentration transfer, a global optimum, caloric performance or adoption of either parameter record. Active bounds, engineering probe intervals, finite-difference quality, the Matin 21 °C versus packet 20 °C convention, source-method differences and the unconverged P4 refits limit interpretation. The original P2/P3 falsifiers concern the historical 160-target gap; they are not redefined after the objective change. The 142-target assessment and comparison section received the [Supported delivered review](https://github.com/tannerpolley/MEA-Thermodynamics/issues/121#issuecomment-5907883147). Physical use remains limited to the owner-selected 30 wt% MEA, 40–80 °C domain; the promotion/views require separate review and are not promoted for manuscript use.

## Canonical loading correction {#canonical-loading-correction}

**Corrected canonical requests conserve the measured CO₂ loading.** For the adopted SSM+DS record `9055458d`, the 104-row, 40–80 °C pressure AARD is 20.581177%; the 21-row canonical 80 °C AARD is 20.270257%. On the same 11 Jou 80 °C rows, the canonical calculation now agrees with the packet calculation at 9.239806% AARD. Original Born also agrees with its packet score, 11.208814%, on those 11 rows. Both records remain below the existing 35% rule. This is numerical verification and assessment on existing observations, not physical validation.

The request's first balance counts elemental carbon, including the two carbons per MEA; its second counts total MEA. Thus measured loading is $(C_{\mathrm{total}}-2n_{\mathrm{MEA,total}})/n_{\mathrm{MEA,total}}$. The old `probe.pressure_observations` assigned measured loading directly to neutral CO₂, while retaining carbamate, bicarbonate and carbonate starting amounts. Their combined CO₂ carbon is $10^{-4}$ mol on the 1 mol MEA basis in every current pressure template. All 161 canonical and 70 transfer requests therefore had loading too high by $10^{-4}$ mol CO₂/mol MEA. At `vle_obs_0203`, the old conserved loading was 0.0175, while the measured and packet loadings are 0.0174.

The builder now changes neutral CO₂ by the difference between desired and template conserved CO₂ carbon before recomputing balances. It accounts for the template's actual ionic seed rather than subtracting a fixed offset. The [231-request carbon comparison](model-d/assessment-p5a-loadfix-carbon-loading.csv) retains measured, old and corrected conserved loadings. The largest corrected loading error is $4.2\times10^{-16}$ mol CO₂/mol MEA. One previous-failure check for `vle_obs_0203` failed on the old builder and passes after correction, with $10^{-12}$ mol absolute tolerance to allow floating-point summation and subtraction error.

| Canonical 80 °C | 21 | 20.282208 → 20.270257 | 20.830943 → 20.914492 |
| Same Jou 80 °C IDs, canonical | 11 | 9.421005 → 9.239806 | 11.208117 → 11.208814 |

The 11 IDs are `vle_obs_0203` through `vle_obs_0213`. Across all 78 pressure rows shared by the packet and canonical cohorts, maximum relative pressure differences are $1.94\times10^{-13}$ for SSM+DS and $2.55\times10^{-13}$ for Original Born, below the existing $10^{-8}$ relative assessment tolerance.

Packet calculations are unaffected: the replay reproduces all checked numeric packet-score fields exactly for each form, including fitted pressure/species scores, costs and carbonate comparisons. The maximum relative difference across those 239 comparisons is $3.10324\times10^{-13}$, below the requested $10^{-8}$ limit; the maximum absolute difference is $1.03959\times10^{-7}$ Pa. Figure pressures are retained in kPa and were multiplied by 1000 for the comparison with assessment pressures in Pa. The [figure provenance](figures/regression_overview/output/provenance.json) retains hashes and comparison numbers. Historical campaigns were not recalculated; `scripts/run_direct_parameter_campaign.py:136` remains outside this correction. ## Assessment of the 142-target records

The following tables retain the assessment before the loading correction. Their canonical and concentration-transfer values for the 142-target records are superseded by the corrected values above; packet calculations remain unchanged.

The completed assessment compares the decision-24 records with the older decision-23 records. ## Decisions

The owner made [decisions 24 and 21 on 30 September 2026](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/121#issuecomment-5906843564). **Decision 24 makes Matin's 18 HCO₃⁻ + CO₃²⁻ pool targets report-only**, based on the authors' high-bicarbonate titration/NMR comparison; Matin's MEA, MEAH⁺ and MEACOO⁻ targets remain fitted. The official objective is now **142 targets**. **Decision 21 chooses SSM+DS**, based on its converged decision-24 cost of 32.991897 against 34.584032 for Original Born, a 4.6% advantage relative to Original Born. The choice is gated on the decision-23 assessment of both 142-target records—104-row 40–80 °C pressure AARD against the 35% limit, packet and canonical completeness, 15/45 wt% transfer, the 80 °C comparison, carbonate against Jakobsen and the indicative NaHCO₃ check—and a **Supported delivered review of that assessment and this comparison section**. The earlier intended adoption scope remains 30 wt% MEA at 40–80 °C; the numerical assessment and [Supported delivered review](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/121#issuecomment-5907883147) are complete. Decision 21’s gate is met; #107 promotes `p5conv-a-11` as the limited-domain working record, while its new promotion/views require separate delivered review.

# Conditional interaction and Born-input sensitivity {#sensitivity-current}

**Under the fixed 142-target objective, removing the MEAH⁺–MEACOO⁻ interaction produces the largest conditional cost increase, while fixing the MEAH⁺–water temperature slope to zero produces the smallest. Born-off refitting converges at cost 98.7914162667, above both Born-form baselines.** All twelve fits converge from the prescribed starts and all final mappings reproduce their native fitted costs. One fixed-input point, SSM+DS at ionic-region relative permittivity 2, remains numerically unavailable; it has no full-objective cost.

This section answers the three questions in [design issue #141](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/141): how interactions compensate after one coordinate is fixed to zero; how fixed Born inputs change agreement without interaction refitting; and how well the five interaction coordinates compensate for removing Born energy while retaining Debye–Hückel electrostatics. The analysis is for conditional sensitivity discussion. Manuscript use requires independent delivered review and investigator promotion of the exact notebook commit. It does not adopt a new parameter record.

## Basis, records and numerical method

The objective retains exactly **48 pressure + 40 Böttinger + 54 Matin targets over 84 states**. Matin's 18 bicarbonate/carbonate-pool observations remain separately labelled report-only. Pressure is CO₂ partial pressure in Pa; species observations use their retained true-species or pooled mole-fraction bases. Loading is mol fed CO₂/mol fed MEA, and 30 wt% denotes the unloaded MEA/water solvent, excluding added CO₂. Pressure fitting remains at 40/60 °C and species retain their measured packet conditions, including the inherited Matin 21 °C measurement versus 20 °C packet convention. No new concentration, thermal or absorber qualification follows.

The input records are SSM+DS `9055458d8b7cd767a0d08e9f37e4fd28631e29c363364d7b842ebade645cb241` and matched Original Born `ebb5f8f9df2aa4ff9bbaec72899dae33fba2233823bb7e389bef92b3d2981900`. The immutable installed Engine wheel is `28181e72e429c6e87fc6361082af1a7b21c8747e76bda65a1c30abb4a97402f2`. All nine species, five reactions, reaction conventions, association topology, neutral interactions, same-sign ion-dispersion exclusion and solvent-only permittivity mixing remain fixed except for the declared perturbation.

The existing scoring functions own pooling, objective membership and residual scales: pressure uses ln(model/observed)/0.3 and species uses (model−observed)/(0.1 observed+0.001); cost is half the sum of squared scaled residuals. These historical engineering scales are not inferred measurement uncertainties. Average absolute relative deviation (AARD) is reported separately on 48 positive pressure observations and 94 positive fitted species observations. Source/species denominators and available counts are retained in the linked tables.

Both Born forms are evaluated at their own matched interaction records. Each SSM+DS interaction ablation uses start A, the adopted vector, and start B, the matched Original Born coordinate vector inserted into the unchanged SSM+DS mapping. The ablated coordinate is exactly zero and omitted from the optimizer; the other four remain free. Intercept ablation retains a free temperature slope, and slope ablation retains a free intercept. Born-off uses the same two starts and all five free coordinates; only Born-specific inputs are removed. Native fitting retains the existing bounds, coordinate scales, exact Engine derivatives and 10⁻¹² relative function stopping criterion, with 40 iterations, 2250 s native elapsed limit and 2400 s external limit. Full evaluations have a 600 s limit and individual states a 180 s limit. Numerical jobs use one thread each, at most two concurrently, after the other worktree's CPU jobs finish.

Böttinger 2008 §§3–7 describe NMR data and coupled chemical/VLE estimation; Matin 2012 Method Description and Speciation Comparisons describe the carbonate-containing bicarbonate profile and ambient-temperature comparisons. Figiel 2025 Model Parameters and Conclusions fit Born diameters, solvent factors and interaction parameters to distinct electrolyte properties, rather than identifying reactive MEA ion values from this objective. These source roles support the measurement and parameter distinctions; they do not supply the numerical tolerances or statistical significance tests used here. [Source identities and reading limits](model-d/sensitivity-current/inputs.json) record current Zotero checks, the unavailable Matin supplement and the Figiel Eq. 7 corrigendum. No new Born equation was transcribed.

No penalty or reduced-target objective is assigned, and no physical nonexistence or proved solver defect is inferred. The permitted one evaluation is exhausted; the cause remains for the existing Engine investigation rather than an additional start or method change in this study.

## Born-off re-calibration

Both Born-off fits converge near **98.7914162667**, with pressure/species AARD **53.903/10.916 %**. They agree in cost and coordinates, but hit HCO₃⁻–water k=+0.5 and MEAH⁺–MEACOO⁻ k=−1. The unchanged reactive problems retain nine species and five reactions. Direct Engine checks at all 168 replayed Born-off liquid states return Born term exactly zero and Debye–Hückel term nonzero; [the term checks](model-d/sensitivity-current/born-off-term-checks.csv) retain the returned fields.

| Start | Reference | Born-off cost | Δpressure | ΔBöttinger | ΔMatin | Δtotal | AARD P / species, % |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | SSM+DS | 98.7914 | 54.8744 | 15.1276 | -4.2024 | 65.7995 | 53.903 / 10.916 |
| A | Original Born | 98.7914 | 51.5810 | 12.4931 | 0.1333 | 64.2074 | 53.903 / 10.916 |

| B | Original Born | 98.7914 | 51.5811 | 12.4930 | 0.1333 | 64.2074 | 53.903 / 10.916 |

The five prescribed interaction coordinates do not recover the Born-form baseline agreement after removing Born energy within the retained bounds and chemistry. Matin cost improves relative to SSM+DS even though pressure and total agreement worsen. This is conditional model-form compensation evidence; it does not isolate or rank Born theories independently of inherited chemistry, fixed ion inputs, data roles or bounds. It does not trigger adoption or bound expansion.

## Numerical evidence, uncertainty and limits

| Check | Declared condition | Retained outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reference replay | ≤10⁻⁸ absolute | both pass |
| Native convergence | existing stopping criterion;40 iterations;2250/2400s | 12/12 converged;15 maximum native history rows;no caps/timeouts |
| Final fitted-map replay | ≤10⁻⁸ absolute;142 targets | 12/12 pass;maximum difference 9.067e-12 |
| Two-start cost agreement | ≤10⁻⁶ relative | maximum 6.713e-13 |
| Two-start k agreement | ≤10⁻⁵ | maximum 2.303e-07 |
| Two-start b agreement | ≤0.1K | maximum 0.000644K |
| Accepted-state material balance | ≤10⁻⁷ mol conserved total | maximum 1.149e-12 |
| Accepted-state charge balance | ≤10⁻⁷ mol charge | maximum 3.184e-13 |
| Accepted-state stationarity | ≤10⁻¹⁰ | maximum 1.592e-12 |
| Full scan availability | 142 fitted targets per comparable point | 35/36 unique mappings complete;εion=2 SSM+DS unavailable |
| Born-off energy and chemistry | Born term0;DH retained;nine species/five reactions | 168/168 term checks pass;declared chemistry/topology unchanged |

The campaign attempts **12 refits and 48 objective evaluation/replay sets**; 47 sets are complete and one scan set is unavailable. Outside optimizer work, **3987 states are attempted, 3986 accepted, one unavailable and 45 deliberately unattempted after that failure**. The nominal 4032 state attempts applies only if every set reaches all 84 states. Native fitting separately records 125 residual and 129 Jacobian evaluations, with no trial failures; those are not added to the state-attempt estimate. Total refit wall time summed across the single-thread jobs is 2667.28 s, and the longest fit is 299.94 s, below every prescribed time limit.

This evidence comprises fixed-input model evaluations, local re-calibration and numerical verification. It does not establish independent physical validation, global optimality, unique physical ion parameters, statistical significance, uncertainty intervals, concentration transfer, thermal/property or absorber qualification, or removal of inherited high-temperature parameter-selection history. Measurement uncertainty, residual-scale choices, fixed-input uncertainty and model discrepancy remain distinct from the measured replay and start differences. Two deterministic starts establish agreement for those starts only.

The retained owners are [frozen inputs, requests and source identities](model-d/sensitivity-current/inputs.json), [ordered targets and measured values](model-d/sensitivity-current/frozen-targets.json), [scan values](model-d/sensitivity-current/born-input-sensitivity-values.csv), [scan target predictions](model-d/sensitivity-current/scan-targets.csv), [final-fit target predictions](model-d/sensitivity-current/fit-replay-targets.csv), [source/species AARD](model-d/sensitivity-current/fit-aard-by-source-species.csv), [native fitting histories](model-d/sensitivity-current/native-fit-summaries.json), [final replay checks](model-d/sensitivity-current/final-replay-checks.json), [start agreement](model-d/sensitivity-current/start-agreement.json), [numerical summary](model-d/sensitivity-current/numerical-summary.json), [Born-off comparisons](model-d/sensitivity-current/born-off-comparison.csv), and [exact numerical commands](model-d/sensitivity-current/execution-commands.json). Bulk state/native outputs remain in the ignored `model-d/sensitivity-current/runs/` directory. All tables and figures above read retained outputs; rendering never reruns the model.

## Born-form ranking after refitting interactions {#ranking-refit}

**The Born-form ranking is input-dependent after both forms refit all five interactions.** SSM+DS has the lower baseline cost, 32.991897 versus 34.584032. At three-ion Born diameters ×0.8, Original Born has the lower converged cost, 31.722527 versus 31.985822. At εMEA = 24, Original Born again has the lower cost, 32.084417 versus 32.896882. The same form does not win at baseline and both altered inputs, so the preregistered “robust ranking” condition is not met.

The [preregistration posted before fitting](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/141#issuecomment-5927291060) was committed locally as `0e7fa72e07a67a5e614ec3bfa094497106641744`. Four cases combine two Born forms with the two fixed input sets; each refits the five interactions from its own accepted coordinates and the matched other-form coordinates. Exactly eight fits were attempted. Two fresh baseline replays and eight final-map replays retain the same 142 targets over 84 states: 48 pressure, 40 Böttinger and 54 Matin. The 18 Matin bicarbonate/carbonate-pool targets remain report-only.

Only MEAH⁺, MEACOO⁻ and HCO₃⁻ Born diameters change in the diameter cases. H₃O⁺, OH⁻ and CO₃²⁻ Born diameters, every packing and Debye–Hückel diameter, and εMEA = 32 stay fixed. The εMEA = 24 cases keep all diameters fixed. Both retain f_water = 1.5, f_MEA = 1, εion = 8, the nine-species/five-reaction chemistry, inherited reaction correlations including source R4, association topology, solvent-only permittivity mixing, neutral interactions and the pinned Engine wheel `28181e72`. Original Born has c_shell = c_dielectric = 0; SSM+DS has both 1. Born remains enabled. The existing fitter's `11`/`00` argument selects starting coordinates only; the supplied input mapping specifies the physical form. Existing shared fit anchors and actual-form final replay anchors remain unchanged.

The objective and residuals are those defined above: C = ½Σr², with pressure log residual scale 0.3 and species scale 0.1x_observed + 0.001. These fixed scales are engineering choices. Pressure is CO₂ partial pressure in Pa, species use retained true-species or pooled mole fractions, loading is mol fed CO₂/mol fed MEA, and 30 wt% is the unloaded solvent basis. Pressure fitting remains at 40/60 °C; species retain their packet temperatures and the inherited Matin 21 °C measurement versus 20 °C packet convention. The three ion–water k bounds remain [−0.5,0.5], the MEAH⁺–MEACOO⁻ bound [−1,1], and the MEAH⁺–water reciprocal-temperature slope bound [−1000,1000] K. No Born input is fitted.

The following table reads the [retained fitted costs](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/fitted-costs.csv). Total/family costs are dimensionless final-replay values; native fitted costs agree within 10⁻⁸. “Own” and “other” describe coordinate starts, with physical form fixed in each pair. AARD means average absolute relative deviation; pressure/species denominators are 48/94 positive observations throughout. H denotes HCO₃⁻–water k = +0.5; C denotes MEAH⁺–MEACOO⁻ k = −1. Baselines replay the retained converged fits and have no new paired-start check. A table preserves these six scalar input/form comparisons and their exact lower-cost decision; a plot adds no further tested response.

Original Born's total advantage at both altered inputs comes from its lower Matin cost; SSM+DS retains lower pressure and Böttinger costs. Allowing interaction compensation therefore preserves the reversal seen against the baseline in the fixed-interaction scans, while showing that it also holds against SSM+DS refitted at the same altered inputs. This is conditional calibration under the declared observation roles and scales, rather than an intrinsic ranking of Born theories.

Across the three tested input sets, the minimum fitted cost is **31.7225274151 for Original Born** and **31.9858215136 for SSM+DS**, both at the three-ion diameter multiplier 0.8. These are minima among the tested cases, with local bounded fits; neither is an optimization over all Born inputs or evidence of global optimality.

All four pairs meet cost agreement ≤10⁻⁶ relative, each k agreement ≤10⁻⁵ and b agreement ≤0.1 K. The [start differences](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/start-agreement.json) are:

| Input | Form | Relative cost difference | Maximum k difference | b difference, K |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Diameters ×0.8 | Original Born | 1.871e-13 | 7.622e-08 | 0.000205 |
| Diameters ×0.8 | SSM+DS | 6.661e-13 | 1.871e-07 | 0.000973 |
| εMEA = 24 | Original Born | 8.615e-14 | 4.062e-08 | 0.000097 |
| εMEA = 24 | SSM+DS | 7.905e-13 | 2.426e-07 | 0.000637 |

All eight native fits converge without trial failures, caps or timeouts. All 840 replayed states meet balance and stationarity limits and retain baseline phase support/topology. Maximum absolute material balance is 1.063e-12 mol; maximum charge balance is 2.477e-13 mol charge; maximum stationarity is 1.521e-12, below 10⁻¹⁰. Maximum native/replay cost difference is 6.374e-12, below 10⁻⁸. All final coordinates meet their retained bounds and k(T) < 1 at 293.15/353.15 K; chemistry and undeclared inputs are unchanged. Native fitting records 70 residual and 66 Jacobian evaluations. Summed single-thread fit wall time is 1541.76 s; the longest fit is 267.48 s, below its 2250 s native/2400 s external limits. Execution used one available host slot while another fit occupied the second, with OMP/OpenBLAS/MKL set to one thread for every study job.

The retained [target predictions and source identities](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/target-predictions.csv), [state checks](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/state-checks.csv), [source/species AARD](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/aard-by-source-species.csv), [native histories and final-mapping filenames](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/native-fit-summaries.json), [numerical summary](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/numerical-summary.json), [ranking and minima](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/ranking.json), [input identities](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/inputs.json), and [commands](model-d/sensitivity-current/ranking-refit/execution-commands.json) support this section. Bulk outputs remain in the ignored `ranking-refit/runs/` directory. Tables are assembled from retained values; rendering never runs the model.

This is re-calibration and numerical verification on the frozen objective. It does not establish independent physical validation, unique physical Born or interaction parameters, statistical significance or uncertainty intervals, concentration/temperature transfer, or absorber qualification. Active bounds, inherited chemistry and parameter-selection history remain limitations. Two starts demonstrate agreement for those starts only. The source basis and reading limits are inherited from the preceding sensitivity section; the relevant Böttinger, Matin and Figiel reading-copy hashes were checked against current Zotero files. Manuscript use requires investigator promotion of this new notebook section after independent delivered review.

The Engine input fields accept a Debye–Hückel diameter record for ionic formulations, but this bundle does not treat it as an independently fitted parameter: the retained ion values are fixed by the convention $d_{DH}=0.88\sigma$. It is therefore omitted from this manuscript-facing parameter table while remaining in the machine-readable records. <span id="note-b">**b**</span> Water segment diameter (Å), with $T$ in K:

$$\sigma_{\mathrm{H_2O}}(T)=2.7927+10.11e^{-0.01775T}-1.417e^{-0.01146T}$$
<span id="note-c">**c**</span> Water relative permittivity, with $T$ in K:

$$\epsilon_{r,\mathrm{H_2O}}(T)=78.4104347858-0.3613376623(T-298.15)+0.000765556183(T-298.15)^2$$

The relative permittivity $\epsilon_r$ supports both ionic and Born contributions; it is grouped under ionic to avoid duplication. Bulk permittivity uses normalized MEA–water mass fractions only; the ion value 8 is retained for the extended Born formulation, and CO₂ is excluded from dielectric mixing. Unique ion Born diameters and the nonunit water solvation factor activate extended Born (SSM+DS). Ion association is absent in this topology; CO₂ retains its induced-association parameters, including zero self-association energy.

The packet-v5 MEA 2B self-association volume is 0.036287. **R1 and R3 · common correlation**

$$
\ln K_{\mathrm{common}}(T)=A+\frac{B}{T}+C\ln T+DT+\Delta
$$

**R2 · CO₂ hydration (recorded correlation, no separate $\Delta$)**

$$
\ln K_2(T)=A_2+\frac{B_2}{T}+C_2\ln T+D_2T
$$

**R4 · carbamate hydrolysis**

$$
\ln K_4(T)=A_4+\frac{B_4}{T}
$$

**R5 · MEAH⁺ dissociation**

$$
\ln K_5(T)=-\ln(10)\left(\frac{A_5}{T}+B_5+C_5T\right)
$$

R2's recorded $A_2$ and $B_2$ already contain both the conversion to aqueous molality (+4.0165 in ln K) and the adopted constant enthalpy shift of −8.2019 kJ mol⁻¹, applied so that ln K is unchanged at the 313.15 K pivot; R2 therefore has no separate $\Delta$ term. At 313.15 K the recorded correlation gives $\ln K_2=-14.5050$.

# Fit statistics {#fit-statistics}

The figure labels and [`results/current-best-fit-ln-statistics.csv`](results/current-best-fit-ln-statistics.csv) compute these from the retained residual rows (calculated against observed value, same state) through one function in `scripts/render_regression_overview.py`; the log₁₀ statistics file and the heat deviations come from their generation scripts and agree with it:

- **n**: number of rows with positive observed and calculated values.
- **bias (mean ln)**: mean of ln(pred/obs); positive means over-prediction on average.
- **RMS ln**: root mean square of ln(pred/obs).
- **log₁₀ RMSE** = RMS ln / ln 10 (RMS ln = 2.303 × log₁₀ RMSE).
- **RMS factor** = exp(RMS ln), the typical multiplicative error.
- **AARD %** = 100 · mean |pred/obs − 1|. AARD is asymmetric: over-prediction by a factor of 2 contributes 100 %, under-prediction by a factor of 2 contributes 50 %.
- **mean dev** (heat only) = mean(calculated − observed) in kJ mol⁻¹ CO₂.

The predecessor MEA and reactive ePC-SAFT papers report the mean absolute relative deviation of CO₂ partial (or total) pressure calculated at the measured loading, printed as AAD %, ARD, AARD, |ΔY/Y| or MAPE, per data set: Baygi 2015 Table 5 [<a href="#ref-11">11</a>], Najafloo 2018 Table 5 [<a href="#ref-3">3</a>], Uyan 2015 Eq. 25 [<a href="#ref-12">12</a>], Wangler 2018 Eq. 32 [<a href="#ref-13">13</a>], Bülow 2021a Eq. 28 [<a href="#ref-14">14</a>], Zhang 2011 Table 9 [<a href="#ref-15">15</a>], Hilliard 2008 Eq. 7-9 and Table 13.4-6 [<a href="#ref-16">16</a>], Aronu 2011 Eq. 21 [<a href="#ref-17">17</a>] and Akula 2023a Eq. 36 [<a href="#ref-18">18</a>]. None reports a log-space RMSE or a signed bias; Akula 2023a fits Σ(ln p_exp − ln p_cal)² but reports MAPE. The per-source pressure table and the figure legends therefore lead with AARD % on pCO₂, the same residual direction (pressure at measured temperature and loading), and keep bias and RMS ln / log₁₀ RMSE as symmetric complements.

Loading-direction statistics are not comparable with pressure AARD: Hilliard 2008 Table 13.4-6 gives 13.55 % on pCO₂ but 0.52 % on loading for Jou 1995 [<a href="#ref-16">16</a>], and Mac Dowell 2010 reports absolute deviations in x_CO₂ [<a href="#ref-19">19</a>]. Published values also cover different row subsets, and most (Zhang 2011, Hilliard 2008, Aronu 2011, Akula 2023a) are calibration values.

## 142-target local identification

The five-column exact weighted physical Jacobian is evaluated at the serialized selected point through the existing native initial-Jacobian path, with **zero optimizer updates**. Physical singular values are 73.9801043, 45.0847435, 25.0537109, 3.93436295, 0.00569527215; these columns mix dimensionless interaction coefficients and the K-valued slope. Column-normalized singular values are 1.55012749, 1.13410791, 0.898647756, 0.698307315, 0.125312071. All five columns are numerically nonzero. The HCO₃⁻–water coordinate remains at its +0.5 upper bound with an outward descent direction (cost gradient -12.467401). Full unconstrained covariance and uncertainty bands are not reported. The [Jacobian table](results/promotion-107-jacobian.csv) and [identification summary](results/promotion-107-identification.json) replace no historical 160-target errors.

Historical 160-target SSM+DS accounting remains six starts attempted, five converged and one failed initial solve. The 142-target record is a warm continuation that converged after one further update, with relative function tolerance 1e−12 and zero trial failures. It is not six independent 142-target starts or evidence of a global optimum.
